title: Tell a Story in 9 Minutes
subtitle: How structure, hooks, and engagement turn a ramble into a story people remember
intro: A reel promises: give me 9 minutes, I'll improve your story. 2.5 million people stopped scrolling to watch.
takeaway: Good storytelling is structure plus a hook that earns attention, then pays it back.

sections.heading: Analogy: Storytelling is hosting on a couch
sections.body:
Imagine you invite a stranger to sit on your couch. A story is how you host them. Story structure is the order you tell things in — beginning, middle, end — so they know where to sit and where you're going.

Without that order, they fidget and leave. With it, they lean in, which is why you need more than just good facts.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? To earn and keep attention
sections.body:
Audience engagement means your listener stays, reacts, and remembers. A story hook is the first 10 seconds that makes them want to stay — a question, a surprise, a promise.

In the reel, a creator talks straight to camera from a couch to model this: start close and personal, then deliver.

A hook gets the click, but structure keeps the watch, and that's where stories break.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When hooks trick but don't deliver
sections.body:
What fails first if your story gets 100x more viewers? A flashy hook with no structure. You get views but no trust, because you promised and didn't pay off.

Another trap is telling for you, not them. If your order makes sense to you but not your audience, engagement drops.

So test one hook and one clear structure before you polish anything else.

steps.narration: You open with a hook — a question or surprise that earns 10 seconds.
You follow a clear structure so the listener knows where you are going.
That order turns attention into engagement and memory.
If you hook without structure, attention collapses and trust breaks.

quiz.q: What is a story hook in this lesson?
options: The first seconds that make you want to stay
The final moral of the story
quiz.why: A hook is the opening that earns attention, like the reel's 9-minute promise.

quiz.q: What breaks first if your story reaches 100x more people but has a hook with no structure?
options: Viewers click but leave quickly and trust drops
quiz.why: A hook without payoff gets clicks but loses retention — engagement fails.

options: To give listeners order so they can follow and remember
quiz.why: Structure is beginning → middle → end so an audience can follow and stay engaged.

judge.why: D3 stays closest to the thin source—9-minute promise, 2.5m views, couch image, and the three named concepts—while defining terms plainly with a clear hook-to-payoff flow. D1 and D2 invent unsupported details like 50 hook templates and, for D1, Kittl, presenting them as saved material.
